title: Schema anchoring & late-binding tool maps: acceptance criteria for streamed structured outputs and function-call error tokens
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Clarify acceptance criteria for a new 'schema anchoring' mechanism and late-binding tool map behavior when the LLM emits streamed structured fragments. Define a compact error-token vocabulary for function/tool-call failures and resume semantics for partial fragments. PRD scope updated to include runtime-side late-binding and resume tests; this ticket captures acceptance checks, required tests, telemetry, and rollback conditions.
scope_changes: Added late-binding tool map: runtime may resolve tool identifiers emitted by the model to concrete tool endpoints at call time (not only at compile time)
Introduce 'schema anchor' frames that mark durable schema checkpoints in a stream; downstream consumers can use anchors to validate and resume from checkpoints
Define a minimal error-token vocabulary (error_frame, retryable_error, fatal_error, unknown_tool, tool_unavailable) communicated inline with fragments
Expanded PRD to require e2e resume and replay tests across model variants and regional routing fallbacks
acceptance_criteria: Schema anchoring: Streams MUST allow anchor frames (type: 'anchor') with a stable anchor_id that binds to a canonical schema version and example payload. Anchor frames are durable and can be acknowledged by the client; when an anchor is present, subsequent fragments MAY omit repeated schema metadata.

Late-binding tool map semantics: When the model emits a tool identifier (tool_id) in a function-call frame, the runtime MAY resolve tool_id to a runtime tool_map entry at execution time. If resolution returns multiple compatible endpoints, runtime must select according to routing policy and annotate the tool_call event with resolved_tool_id and resolved_endpoint in telemetry.

Tool-call handshake: Before invoking an external tool, the runtime MUST emit a tool_call.handshake event (synchronous) and accept an explicit OK/DECLINE response from the tool gateway. If DECLINE, the runtime must convert to a fallback model action per policy (fallback_model or error_frame).

Error-token semantics: The stream-level error tokens MUST be one of the defined vocabulary and include an error_code, human_readable message, and optional resume_token when retryable. Clients must be able to distinguish retryable vs fatal without schema parsing (i.e., token prefix 'retry:' vs 'fatal:').

Partial fragment resume: If a stream is interrupted mid-fragment, clients MUST be able to request a resume using the latest anchor_id and resume_token. The runtime MUST support resuming from anchor_ids in the last 30s for hosted flows (configurable for Dedicated).

Idempotency for tool calls: Every tool_call frame MUST include an idempotency_key. Tool gateways MUST accept duplicate idempotency_keys within the window specified by the runtime and return canonical result or a 2xx duplicate acknowledgment. Acceptance tests will validate duplicate suppression across retries.

Fallback model invocation: If a tool is unavailable or DECLINE occurs, the runtime MUST either (a) invoke a configured fallback_model variant or (b) emit an error_frame with clearly scoped remediation steps. The chosen behavior must be deterministic and documented in the route config.

Streaming schema validation: Runtime MUST validate emitted fragments against the active anchored schema when possible; schema deviations MUST produce a structured 'schema_violation' error_frame rather than raw text. Validation must not block low-latency paths for best-effort routes (labelled 'low-latency-unsafe').

Observability: Each tool_call and anchor checkpoint MUST emit traces with anchor_id, resolved_tool_id, idempotency_key, latencies, and error_token. These fields MUST appear in Console traces and the per-route dashboard within the release window.
Backward compatibility: Streams that do not emit anchors MUST still be supported. Acceptance includes regression tests ensuring >95% compatibility with pre-anchor consumers in the regression suite.
e2e_tests: Resume scenario: simulate network cut after a complex nested fragment, then resume using anchor_id + resume_token; assert final stitched object equals non-interrupted baseline
Tool-unavailable scenario: runtime resolves tool_id to an endpoint that returns DECLINE; assert fallback_model invoked and response schema matches expectation
Duplicate tool-call: replay same idempotency_key across 3 retries; assert single effective execution recorded in telemetry and client receives consistent result
Schema-violation detection: model emits fragment violating anchored schema; assert runtime emits 'schema_violation' error_frame and client receives clear diagnostics
Latency guardrails: under burst load, runtime must preserve 'low-latency-unsafe' routing behavior and not block streaming validation; measure p95 token latency against baseline
telemetry_requirements: Emit anchor lifecycle events: anchor.emit, anchor.ack, anchor.resume_attempt, anchor.resume_result
Emit tool_call events including resolved_tool_id, resolved_endpoint, idempotency_key, and failure_reason
Expose counts of retryable vs fatal error_tokens per route and per-model-version in Console within 24 hours
Synthetic test results (resume/test harness) must be stored as a named dashboard and alert if failure rate >1% over 1 hour
notes: Design tradeoff: anchor frames add metadata overhead but simplify resume semantics and validation; default anchor cadence proposed: 1 per 2KB emitted or every 3s, whichever first
Security: late-binding tool maps increase surface area for misrouting; runtime will validate tool_map entries against allowlists and require signed manifests for Private deployments
Operational: Dedicated customers may configure longer resume windows; default hosted window set to 30s to bound memory/kv-cache retention costs
